articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. to Make Vikings Debut on MNF vs. Bills After Latest Rumors on Contract Status
articles.summary: After spending the past month on the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad, veteran wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. will finally get his chance to see some game action.
articles.body:
After spending the past month on the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad, veteran wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. will finally get his chance to see some game action.

Beckham will be active for his team's Week 9 game against the Buffalo Bills:

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero first reported on Sunday that the Vikings were signing Beckham to the 53-man roster ahead of their Monday Night Football game.

The Vikings have an opening on offense after veteran wideout Jauan Jennings was ruled out for Monday night's game after suffering a strained calf in practice this week. His injury came after star quarterback Kyler Murray was sidelined with a hamstring injury, thrusting veteran backup Carson Wentz into the starting role against the Bills.

Beckham started the 2026 season with the New York Giants, but he didn't record a single catch in any of the three games he played before he was released in late September. He signed with Minnesota's practice squad a week after his departure from New York.

ESPN's Kevin Seifert reported on Saturday that Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said the team is "working through whether [Beckham] will be active Monday night." The Bills rank 24th in the NFL with 352.1 yards allowed per game, so Wentz would benefit from having an extra weapon against a subpar defense.

Minnesota is coming off its first loss of the season last week against the Detroit Lions, and Murray's absence will certainly make things more difficult against Buffalo. If Beckham gets his chance on the main roster, he will certainly be motivated to prove that he deserves to stay.

articles.title: Puka Nacua Injury Update, Latest News and Timeline After Rams WR Hurt on Final Play vs. Commanders
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams will be without Puka Nacua for an extended stretch, head coach Sean McVay told reporters Monday:
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without Puka Nacua for an extended stretch, head coach Sean McVay told reporters Monday:

Nacua is going on injured reserve, which will keep him out for a minimum of four weeks.

Rams to Consider Trade After Puka Injury

Nacua suffered the knee injury on the final offensive snap of the 20-13 win against the Washington Commanders, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sunday:

On Monday, McVay discussed his regret on the final play call:

The injury came after a monster day for Nacua, who hauled in 14 receptions for a season-high 150 yards and a touchdown, marking his third consecutive game finding the end zone.

Nacua stayed healthy last year en route to the best season of his career, in which he recorded 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns, but injuries struck early on in the 2026 campaign.

After playing in the first game of the season against the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, he missed Weeks 2 and 3 against the New York Giants and Denver Broncos, respectively, because of a groin injury.

Despite having to miss two games, Nacua has put together another strong season, recording 715 yards and four touchdowns on 70 receptions.

Another injury to Nacua represents a major blow to a Rams offense that is already without one of its key players.

Veteran wide receiver Davante Adams landed on the injured reserve after Los Angeles' Week 6 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. The initial timeline for his return was six to 10 weeks, though head coach Sean McVay said in late October that Adams is expected to return "on the shorter end" of that frame.

Tight end Terrance Ferguson has also missed time with a hamstring injury .

When healthy, the pairing of Nacua and Adams is one of the best in the league and gives the Rams arguably the scariest offense in the NFL. Los Angeles is finally getting things going after winning three straight games, and it will look to keep the momentum going with or without its top two receivers.

articles.title: Baker Mayfield makes bold accusation against Chicago Bears after Buccaneers’ loss leaves questions unanswered
articles.summary: Baker Mayfield left the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ loss to the Chicago Bears with more than frustration over the result.
articles.body: Baker Mayfield left the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ loss to the Chicago Bears with more than frustration over the result. The quarterback questioned the Bears’ defensive line for what he viewed as activity around the snap that made it harder for Tampa Bay to avoid penalties. The Buccaneers were flagged for five false starts in the Week 9 defeat, and Mayfield’s comments shifted attention toward Chicago’s tactics. But that explanation did not erase the larger issue: Tampa Bay also committed two delay-of-game penalties, giving its offense too many ways to fall behind the chains.Baker Mayfield points to the Bears’ cadence tacticsBaker Mayfield said he could not fully explain why the Buccaneers had so many false starts, stressing that the number was out of character. He did, however, single out the Bears’ defensive line for allegedly calling out the cadence between snaps.“To be honest with you, I don’t know,” said Mayfield on why the team had so many false startse start penalties. “The last one. I know they’re barking out the cadence. Which you can’t do that. So it’s tough for the refs to call that because they’re not right there at the line of scrimmage. But yeah, I think they called that on Tristan, but that’s, you can’t do that.”Mayfield believed the defenders were trying to disrupt Tampa Bay’s timing by shouting during the pre-snap sequence. He also suggested officials had a difficult view because they were not directly along the line of scrimmage. That is his account, not an official finding that Chicago broke a rule.The Buccaneers still had to manage their own operation. Five false starts are a heavy cost for any offense, regardless of the defense’s tactics. Two delay-of-game penalties added to the damage, turning chances to go for it into field-goal attempts.Bowles puts the focus back on Tampa BayHead coach Todd Bowles did not follow Mayfield in blaming Chicago. He said the penalties were not caused by a communication breakdown, but made clear that Tampa Bay needed to control its movement before the snap.“It wasn’t a communication thing,” Bowles said post-game. “We just got to hold our water.”Bowles’ response pointed to the standard Tampa Bay has to meet. A defense can use noise and cadence disruption to make life difficult. The offense still has to stay composed, identify the snap count and avoid giving away free yards. The Buccaneers cannot build their operation around expecting a flag.That difference in tone is worth noting. Mayfield was describing what he believed the Bears were doing; Bowles was judging what his own players could control. The coach did not need to settle whether Chicago’s defenders were trying to draw a reaction. His team had already been penalized, and the result was clear. False starts put the offense behind schedule before a play could develop. Delay-of-game calls then removed options on later downs. Those are separate errors, but together they point to an offense that struggled to get set and execute cleanly.The loss leaves Tampa Bay at 3-6 after a season that had shown signs of turning. The Buccaneers began 0-3, then went 1-2 with Jalon Daniels at quarterback before Mayfield started the next two wins. That lift has faded, even with the NFC South still within reach.Tampa Bay has a bye before facing the Detroit Lions in Week 11. The break offers time to reset, but the offense needs more than a debate over the Bears’ cadence. Mayfield may feel Chicago crossed a line. Bowles’ message was simpler: Tampa Bay has to stop making the mistakes itself.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How the Chiefs won the second half 21-0: Travis Kelce’s third-quarter TD turned a two-point edge into an eight-point cushion and never let New York Jets back in
articles.summary: Kansas City led by two at halftime and had just heard a stadium full of boos.
articles.body: Kansas City led by two at halftime and had just heard a stadium full of boos. Harrison Butker had missed from 56 and 51 yards on back-to-back tries to close the half, and the Jets were still within a score. Then the Chiefs got the ball to start the third quarter and went to work. Travis Kelce took a fourth-and-goal flip from Patrick Mahomes at the 1-yard line and powered in. Kansas City won the second half 21-0 and finished with a 35-12 victory at Arrowhead on Sunday. New York never got closer.Travis Kelce’s goal-line score turned the game for Kansas CityPatrick Mahomes looked ready to sneak it. Instead he flipped the ball to Kelce, who bulled across the line behind blocks from tight ends Jake Briningstool and Noah Gray and receiver Jalen Royals. The score made it 20-12, the biggest lead either team had held all day, and Butker’s extra point pushed it to 21-12.The drive was built on Kenneth Walker. Andy Reid had given him five carries in the whole first half. Out of the break, Reid fixed that. Walker touched the ball five times on one possession, with runs of 11, 8 and 12 yards.Short yardage had been a worry for Kansas City. Backup quarterback Justin Fields lost a fumble on an early sneak, and the offense had to prove it could fix that. It did. The Chiefs converted 5 of 8 tries on third or fourth down with 3 yards or fewer to go, and Kelce’s score and a late touchdown by Emmett Johnson were part of that. All four trips inside the red zone ended in touchdowns. Walker finished with 143 yards and three scores, two of them catches from Mahomes, after two straight games under 100 yards.The Jets had no answer after halftimeNew York had nothing left. The Jets gained negative 9 yards in the third quarter, according to Athlon Sports, and they ran for just 7 yards after halftime. They never reached the end zone all day. They led 6-0 early and 9-7 in the second quarter. Their points came from four Jason Sanders field goals, from 23, 48, 49 and 54 yards. The first came after an eight-minute opening drive that stalled at the Kansas City 5.The pass rush finally showed up. Geno Smith came in with 23 sacks taken, tied for second most in the league. Kansas City added five more, including two each from Chris Jones and George Karlaftis. Before Sunday, the Chiefs ranked in the bottom third of the NFL in pressure rate.Mahomes did it with a sore right elbow. It was crushed mid-game, and he still finished with 242 yards and two touchdowns.The Chiefs were cleaner, too. They took three accepted penalties for 20 yards, while the Jets took nine for 57.Kansas City is 6-2 and visits Atlanta next Sunday, but two loose ends remain. Reid told CBS at the break he wanted to see a field goal go through in the second half. Butker did not attempt another one, so the kicker question is still open. The other is receiver. Xavier Worthy left late with a lower-body injury, and the trade deadline arrives Tuesday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL Monday Night Football preview: Vikings defense gets a tough test vs. Josh Allen and Bills
articles.summary: The No. 1 defense in the NFL this season has a big challenge on Monday night.
articles.body:
Josh Allen has been the best quarterback in the NFL this season, at least by some key metrics. But he hasn't faced a defense like the Minnesota Vikings.

And the Vikings have been the best defense in the NFL. Yet, they haven't faced a quarterback like Allen.

The Vikings host the Buffalo Bills on Monday night in a fun matchup of 6-1 teams. Allen's ability to beat the Vikings' many blitzes will be the key to this game. Nobody else has done it. The Chicago Bears are on a roll offensively, but the Bears scored just three points at home against the Vikings' aggressive defense in Week 2. Minnesota has allowed the lowest EPA ( expected points added ) per play among all NFL defenses this season. Allen has the highest EPA per play among all quarterbacks.

While the headlining matchup will be Allen against the Vikings' defense led by coordinator Brian Flores, there will be intrigue when the Vikings have the ball too. The Vikings' offense, led by Carson Wentz as regular starting quarterback Kyler Murray sits out with a sore hamstring, will have to find a way to move the ball. Minnesota is 6-1 despite being 27th in points per game and 29th in yards per game. Murray has been a big disappointment, and perhaps the Vikings didn't want to rush him back from the hamstring injury to see if Wentz can give the offense a spark. It's possible against a suspect Bills defense that has allowed the third-most passing yards per game this season.

But everyone will be tuning in to see what Allen, the former MVP, does against Minnesota. With a big game, Allen will remain at the front of the pack to win another MVP award. And Buffalo will look like an even stronger Super Bowl contender.

The 2026 NFC North looks like a division that could send all four teams to the playoffs. It's deep from top to bottom. Even though the Vikings are 6-1, they can't feel safe with the Bears, Packers and Lions all playing well. The Bills also will be pushed in the AFC East by the Patriots, but New England lost on Sunday and is three games behind Buffalo in the loss column. Both 6-1 teams are in good shape even with a loss, and will look even stronger with a win. Because of the Vikings' competition within their division — and to a lesser extent, their quest to get the respect of being a legitimate Super Bowl contender — Minnesota needs it a little more.

The Vikings lost their last game at Detroit, with Jefferson having multiple passes thrown far off target to him, and he left the locker room without speaking to the media afterward. That was a clear sign he was upset. This week, Kyler Murray will sit out with a sore hamstring, leading to speculation he is being "soft benched." Even if that's not the case, having Carson Wentz at quarterback could help Jefferson, one of the league's best receivers who has been held back by bad quarterback play each of the last two seasons. The Bills are a good matchup for Jefferson. They've already allowed 1,078 yards and 11 touchdowns to receivers this season, via CBS . Getting Jefferson going again could revitalize a struggling Vikings offense.

The Vikings will be a home underdog for the first time this season when they take on Josh Allen and the 6-1 Bills. Some respected action has dropped the number from Bills -3.5 down to -3, but the betting public is overwhelmingly on Buffalo. Minnesota will give Carson Wentz the start in hopes that he can spark a bottom-five offense. Will he be able to get Justin Jefferson the ball and help run the offense? Minnesota's defense has been incredible so far, but even it has its limits. This should be a fun one. — Ben Fawkes

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

Week 9 will have a fascinating ending, as Buffalo's loaded offense takes on Minnesota's nasty defense. Here are three fantasy themes to track as you watch the game.

1. Will Carson Wentz stabilize the Minnesota passing game? The Vikings scratched Kyler Murray ostensibly with a hamstring injury, but it's also possible this is a soft benching of sorts. Wentz is obviously past his prime at age 34, but he's an experienced player who might be better served to keep the offense on schedule. Justin Jefferson would surely appreciate that.

2. Can DJ Moore keep rolling? When healthy, Moore has been just what the Buffalo passing game needed, with three outstanding games out of five. But the Minnesota defense has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing WRs. Moore and TE Dalton Kincaid (11.5 yards per target) are the best downfield options for QB Josh Allen, but this is the hardest opponent they've faced yet.

3. How will the Vikings handle the backfield? Jordan Mason was the primary back two weeks ago, but neither Mason or Aaron Jones got to 10 touches in the ugly loss to Detroit. Jones still has a better YPC and Mason doesn't have a catch yet this year, but Jones is also five years older. You understand why Jonathan Taylor is occasionally linked to the Vikings. — Scott Pianowski

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys’ last-minute win over Indianapolis Colts won’t hide the bigger problem facing Jerry Jones and Brian Schottenheimer
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys escaped with a 24-21 win over the Indianapolis Colts, but the narrow result did little to ease the pressure on Jerry Jones and head
articles.body: The Dallas Cowboys escaped with a 24-21 win over the Indianapolis Colts, but the narrow result did little to ease the pressure on Jerry Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Dallas needed a late push to avoid another damaging loss, with Brandon Aubrey delivering the winning field goal as time expired. The victory offered some relief after a difficult stretch, yet it also exposed a familiar problem. The Cowboys continue to make games harder than they need to be, raising questions about whether this team has the consistency and discipline to compete when the stakes rise.Dallas’ penalties and poor decisions nearly cost them against IndianapolisDallas had several chances to take control, yet repeated mistakes kept Indianapolis in the game. The Cowboys committed 14 penalties for 153 yards, a costly total that turned promising moments into fresh problems. CeeDee Lamb’s fumble added to the frustration, while the offense struggled to maintain its rhythm.Rookie defensive back Caleb Downs gave Dallas a vital lift with a late interception and an important tackle during the closing minutes. The defense also showed signs of improvement, but the bigger picture remains troubling. The Cowboys have now allowed at least 20 points in 16 consecutive weeks, setting a franchise record. One strong finish cannot erase that pattern.The win also raises questions about Schottenheimer’s decisions. His play-calling has come under scrutiny, and Dallas often seemed to undo its own progress through poor discipline. Against a Colts team that has already traded away key players and is considering further moves, the Cowboys should have found a more convincing way to win.That is what makes the result hard to celebrate without reservations. Dallas showed enough talent to pull through, but too many of its problems came from within. Those mistakes will be harder to survive against stronger opponents.Jerry Jones faces a bigger decision about Brian SchottenheimerJones has defended his coaching staff, but the narrow victory does little to settle the debate about Schottenheimer’s future. Firing a coach midseason can disrupt a team, particularly when there is no clear interim replacement. Still, keeping a coach simply because the alternatives are limited is hardly a convincing long-term plan.The timing matters. Dak Prescott remains a high-level quarterback, and Dallas has quality players across its roster. But Prescott is in his age-33 season, and the team cannot assume this group will stay together indefinitely. CeeDee Lamb is approaching his late twenties, while key defensive pieces are also moving deeper into their careers.Jones’ decision to limit spending on the head coaching position now looks especially risky. A stronger coaching setup might have helped Dallas turn its talent into a more reliable team. Instead, the Cowboys remain stuck discussing basic execution despite having players capable of much more.Their next game against San Francisco will offer a tougher test. The 49ers have maintained their competitiveness through injuries and have benefited from a stable coaching structure. Dallas will need more than a late kick to keep pace.The win keeps the Cowboys moving, but it does not solve the question hanging over the organization. Jones must decide whether the current staff can make better use of the roster before another season slips away. Beating Indianapolis bought Schottenheimer time. It did not prove he is the right man to lead Dallas forward.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFC North: Is this the best division in football history?
articles.summary: The NFC North is on pace to post the best combined winning percentage of any division in NFL history.
articles.body:
After the NFC West's Seattle Seahawks barely edged out division rival Los Angeles in last year's conference championship and went on to win the Super Bowl, the prevailing wisdom heading into 2026 was that the NFC West would be football's dominant division. Between Seattle, Los Angeles and always-dangerous San Francisco, what could possibly beat the NFC West's 1-2-3 punch?

A 1-2-3-4 punch, as it turns out. The NFC North is one Minnesota Monday night victory away from posting a fully undefeated week for the first time all season. The division as a whole is 25-8, and on pace to claim the unofficial but still badass title of Greatest Division in NFL History.

All four teams have won in vastly different ways — the Vikings by suffocating defense, the Bears by creative chaos, the Lions with high-stakes gambling, and the Packers with sustained improvement every week. The last-place team in the division, 6-3 Green Bay, would lead both the NFC East and NFC South.

At the moment, all four NFC North teams — Vikings (6-1 pending Monday night's game vs. Buffalo), Bears (7-2), Lions (6-2) and Packers — are in playoff position. If they can hold on — and the Packers are a game ahead of the Rams and Seahawks for the No. 7 slot — that would mark the first time that all of a division's teams reached the playoffs. (Three divisions sent four teams to the playoffs back when conferences only had three divisions apiece.)

When we turn to history, the NFC North is competing with, well … itself. The winningest division in NFL history, by both sheer games and winning percentage, is the 2024 NFC North, which won 45 combined games. That was the season of the 15-2 Lions and 14-3 Vikings, and the total winning percentage (45-23, .662) reigns supreme in NFL history even with the 5-12 Bears dragging them down. (Chicago would get better.)

Prior to 2024, you wouldn't guess the best division if I gave you 10 chances. It was the AFC South. Really. Back in 2007, the AFC South featured three playoff teams (13-3 Indianapolis, 11-5 Jacksonville and 10-6 Tennessee), and last-place Houston was still solid enough across the season to post an 8-8 record. That crew totaled a 42-22 record (.656) over the whole season.

The 2013 NFC West, which included 13-3 Seattle, 12-4 San Francisco, 10-6 Arizona and 7-9 St. Louis, also went 42-22, but sent only two teams to the playoffs.

In order for the 2026 NFC North to break its own record, the division will need to win at least 21 games over the season's final eight weeks. That's nearly three wins a week, with the added hurdle that many of those games — at least three per team — are against fellow divisional opponents.

Before anyone in the North gets too high on those gaudy standings numbers, it's worth remembering that divisional success doesn't necessarily forecast playoff triumph. That 2024 NFC North crew went a combined 0-3 in the playoffs, sputtering to three ugly defeats. The 2007 AFC South couldn't manage to send one of its teams to the conference championship; Jacksonville notched the only playoff victory out of that crew. The 2022 NFC East claimed three playoff spots, and the Eagles eventually lost to the Chiefs in Super Bowl LVII. The 2013 NFC West did produce the eventual Super Bowl champion in Seattle, and the Seahawks had to go through division-mate San Francisco to get there.

Unsurprisingly, the four NFC North teams have the toughest remaining strength of schedules, per Tankathon … because they'll all spend the next 10 weeks whomping on each other, with teams like San Francisco and Buffalo mixed in. (The NFC North drew the AFC East as its cross-conference opponent, which means a couple favorable games against Miami and the Jets, but also a planned date with the Bills.)

Looming over and above all this talk is the simple truth that there's not a player, team or fan in the entire NFL who gives a damn about a division's combined success. This isn't college football, where (some) SEC fans will cheer on whichever conference representative is facing off against a dastardly outsider. NFL divisions are an organizational structure, not a source of civic pride.

The key to all this "best division ever" talk is how it impacts the teams when they arrive in the playoffs. Is this a case of iron sharpening iron, as the cliché goes, or fattening up on the high-calorie, low-nutrient fast food that lines the bottom of the NFL? We won't know for certain until January, but the NFC North as a whole is on the right path, no matter where it ends.

articles.title: Browns HC Addresses Shedeur Sanders, Deshaun Watson QB1 Status amid Latest NFL Rumors
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns have not yet named a starting quarterback for their next game against the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns have not yet named a starting quarterback for their next game against the Houston Texans.

"I really haven't thought through it other than getting through this morning's tape," head coach Todd Monken told reporters on Monday. "We just got done meeting with the guys, they'll flush the game and then we'll have a chance to meet offensively more extensively a little bit later today."

Shedeur Sanders started in place of the injured Deshaun Watson in Week 9. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Monday the team was planning to turn back to the veteran Watson.

However, it seems the question remains in doubt.

Cleveland leaned on Shedeur Sanders as the starter for Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints after a concussion limited Watson's availability in practice leading up to the game.

Sanders went 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns against New Orleans. A big chunk of his overall output (124 yards) came on a pair of completions to Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion.

The second-year signal-caller wasn't perfect but seemingly did enough to warrant another look. Hall of Fame coach Bill Cowher was among those lobbying on Sanders' behalf:

In addition to what Sanders put on tape in Week 9, Watson didn't make a compelling argument for himself prior to the concussion. In eight starts, he's averaging 225.8 yards per game and has been sacked 33 times.

The three-time Pro Bowler isn't as sharp as he was during his peak with the Houston Texans, and he looks particularly shaky in the face of pressure.

For what it's worth, Monken did confirm that a player could lose a starting job while being out for injury.

"It's week to week," the coach said . "A player doesn't lose or win a job ... I don't know what that means. Each week we put the best players on the field that give us a chance to win."

The Browns are in the thick of the AFC playoff race at 5-4, and coach Todd Monken will be operating with that in mind, rather than developing one player long term.

articles.title: Falcons reportedly trade safety Jessie Bates III to Jaguars for 2 draft picks, also get Davon Godchaux
articles.summary: Jessie Bates is reportedly on his way to the Jaguars.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons have apparently decided to play for the future. A day after falling to the Cincinnati Bengals 34-17 in Madrid , the Falcons reportedly traded safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars for two draft picks, according to ESPN.

Jacksonville will give up a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick in exchange for Bates.

That wasn't the only move the team made Monday, as it also reportedly acquired New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux in a deal, according to The Ringer. The Jaguars gave up a sixth-round pick in exchange for Godchaux.

Bates has a pretty lengthy history of success in the NFL. Though Bates has made just one Pro Bowl in his career, he's been selected to three All-Pro second teams. His most recent selection came last season, when he made 98 tackles for the Falcons.

Bates, 29, is having another excellent start in 2026. Through nine games, he's registered 60 tackles and three forced fumbles. He'll take those skills to an already-dominant Jaguars defense, which is allowing the second-fewest points per game.

It cost Jacksonville a heavy price, especially considering Bates is in the final year of his contract. Barring an extension, he'll be a free agent at the end of the 2026 season.

But Jacksonville can sense the current roster has Super Bowl upside. Thanks to a tough defense and explosive offense, the Jaguars are 6-2 coming out of Week 9. While other AFC teams have been impressive, the Jaguars might have the best all-around team in the league. The addition of Bates should only help bolster that claim.

For the Falcons, the move signals the team will likely play for 2027. After Sunday's loss to the Bengals, the Falcons dropped to 3-6 on the season.

With the playoffs unlikely, the Falcons will start selling off any player who won't play a significant role with the team moving forward. Bates was the first — and could be the biggest — name traded as the team shifts its focus to the future.

articles.title: Grant Cohn proposes Brandon Aiyuk for George Pickens trade as 49ers face major decision before NFL trade deadline
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers insider Grant Cohn has suggested a surprising trade involving Brandon Aiyuk and Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens.
articles.body: San Francisco 49ers insider Grant Cohn has suggested a surprising trade involving Brandon Aiyuk and Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens. With Aiyuk seeking NFL reinstatement and his future in San Francisco still uncertain, Cohn believes the 49ers should consider swapping him for Pickens. His suggestion comes just before the November 10 trade deadline, while Kyle Shanahan’s team continues dealing with several receiver problems.Grant Cohn wants Kyle Shanahan to trade Brandon Aiyuk for George PickensCohn shared his idea on X ahead of Tuesday’s 4 p.m. ET trade deadline, writing, “Brandon Aiyuk for George Pickens straight up.”The suggestion comes at a difficult time for Aiyuk, who has not played since suffering a serious knee injury in October 2024. He was placed on the 49ers’ reserve/left squad list after a dispute with the team over his recovery and participation in team activities.However, Aiyuk recently took a step toward returning to football by filing paperwork for reinstatement. His new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, confirmed that the receiver was healthy and ready to play. Aiyuk also visited the 49ers’ facility on Friday, November 6, to meet with team officials.“I’m back to 100 percent and looking to get reinstated into the National Football League,” Aiyuk said.Head coach Kyle Shanahan, however, did not sound interested in bringing him back into the team’s plans.“I could care less,” Shanahan said. “It’s been over for our football team for a long time.”The situation has become more complicated because the NFL has reportedly told Aiyuk to repay around $13 million in bonuses to San Francisco. According to The Associated Press, the money is linked to his previous contract bonuses. The 49ers had also voided $27 million in guaranteed money after the receiver failed to take part in required team activities.George Pickens trade proposal comes as 49ers deal with receiver injuriesWhile Aiyuk’s future remains uncertain, the 49ers have their own reasons to look for help at wide receiver. San Francisco entered Week 9 with a 7-1 record but was missing several important players.Mike Evans was dealing with an Achilles injury, Deebo Samuel was out with a hamstring problem, Ricky Pearsall had been ruled out for the season, and Christian Kirk was on injured reserve.The team still managed a 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, with Jordan Watkins stepping up. He caught four passes for 86 yards and scored his first career touchdown on a 37-yard play. Brandin Cooks also remained an option for the offense.Pickens, meanwhile, is playing for Dallas under a one-year, $27.3 million franchise tag after the Cowboys failed to reach a long-term agreement with him before the July deadline. His contract situation makes his future an important subject, but there is no confirmation that Dallas is interested in trading him.Aiyuk has recorded 294 catches for 4,305 yards and 25 touchdowns in 69 games with San Francisco. However, his long absence and the ongoing contract dispute make any potential deal complicated.With the trade deadline approaching, Cohn’s suggestion gives the 49ers another possible option to consider. Still, a straight swap remains an idea from the insider, not a reported agreement between the two teams.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Browns decline to name starting QB for Week 10 after report Deshaun Watson would return
articles.summary: Shedeur Sanders nearly led the Browns to a win in his first start of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Shedeur Sanders got his first start of the 2026 NFL season in Week 9 … and he may be in for another one. A day after Sanders nearly led the team to an overtime victory, Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken refused to name a starter for Week 10.

Monken's comments come after an early report Monday suggested Deshaun Watson would return to the starting lineup vs. the Houston Texans.

Watson — who previously started every game for the Browns this season — missed the team's Week 9 overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints due to a concussion. Though Watson cleared concussion protocol Friday, the team held him out of Sunday's game.

With Watson healthy, an early report Monday suggested he would start for the team in Week 10, per ESPN. But Monken wouldn't commit to that, though the coach may be keeping things quiet for gamesmanship purposes.

In Watson's absence, Sanders threw for 297 yards and two passing touchdowns in a narrow 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. Sanders was nearly the hero of the game, finding tight end Harold Fannin on a 39-yard touchdown in overtime to bring the deficit to one point.

But the Browns decided against playing for the tie, and went for a potential game-winning two-point conversion with just over three minutes to play in overtime. Sanders' pass to wideout Denzel Boston fell incomplete, however, resulting in the Browns losing the game.

While Sanders' numbers look OK, the shift back to Watson makes sense. The veteran led the team to a 5-3 record in eight starts. His numbers haven't been elite — Watson has seven touchdowns and three interceptions on the year — but he's managed games effectively enough to pick up victories.

On top of that, Watson would face his former franchise if he returned to the starting lineup this week. That might give both the quarterback and head coach some added motivation to get Watson back in the starting lineup.

After starting seven games for the Browns down the stretch last season, Sanders hasn't received much playing time in 2026. Since losing a training camp battle to Watson, Sanders had attempted just three passes prior to Sunday's start against the Saints.

With the loss, the Browns dropped to 5-4 on the season. The playoffs are still in play, which could lead to the franchise turning things back over to Watson.

No matter what decision the Browns make, Sanders will likely play a role with the franchise down the stretch. If Cleveland falls out of the hunt or Watson falters, the team has every incentive to give Sanders a long look. With Watson's contract up after the season, the Browns need to figure out whether Sanders is a player worth building around or if another quarterback needs to be brought in for 2027.

articles.title: Packers RB Josh Jacobs needs surgery on fractured finger, could end up on injured reserve
articles.summary: Jacobs fractured his finger during Sunday's win over the Patriots. He missed the first six games of the season on the commissioner's exempt list.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs left during the first half of Sunday's 45-27 victory over the New England Patriots with a fractured finger.

On Monday, head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that Jacobs will require surgery to repair the fracture and didn't rule out a stint on injured reserve. Placement on injured reserve would require Jacobs to miss a minimum of four games.

Jacobs appeared to sustain the injury while stiff-arming safety Craig Woodson as his fingers got caught in Woodson's facemask.

Jacobs left for the locker room, then returned to the sideline, where he appeared to have his injured finger wrapped. But he didn't re-enter the game and instead went back to the locker room. A committee of Packers backs handled carries in his absence.

The Packers listed him as questionable for the remainder of the game but he didn't return. LaFleur said afterward that Jacobs had fractured his finger and the team hoped to find a way for him to play with the injury going forward. It turns out that Jacobs will not be able to play through the injury.

LaFleur said Monday that Jacobs wanted to play through the injury Sunday, but "had no grip strength" in his injured hand.

Jacobs returned to the lineup in Week 7 in a loss to the Lions after sitting six games on the commissioner's exempt list due to an offseason arrest for an alleged domestic incident . He pleaded no contest to charges of battery and criminal damage to property in September.

In two games since his return prior to Sunday's game, Jacobs has tallied 75 rushing yards and one touchdown on 2.3 yards per carry and 11 catches for 68 yards and two more touchdowns.

articles.title: Chris Mara Admits Giants Passed On J.J. McCarthy For Maturity
articles.summary: Giants exec Chris Mara reveals why New York skipped J.J. McCarthy in 2024, then explains how life changes turned him into a key player for the team.
articles.body:
The New York Giants originally passed on J.J. McCarthy during the 2024 NFL Draft, but senior vice president Chris Mara now says the team got the player's mindset wrong. Mara admitted the organization loved the quarterback's physical tools but worried about his maturity coming out of college. Those concerns faded after McCarthy married and had a child, transforming him into a leader the Giants now rely on heavily.

Giants fans watched the team select receiver Malik Nabers with the sixth overall pick instead of taking the quarterback from Michigan. The organization had seriously considered McCarthy before making that choice. In an interview with The New York Post's Steve Serby, Mara clarified the hesitation. He noted that while the skill set was elite, the front office was not sure about the young man's character at the time.

Chris Mara, brother of team CEO John Mara and senior vice president of player personnel for the Giants, discussed the initial draft process exclusively. He revealed that the scouting report on McCarthy was split between high praise for his arm and doubt about his life choices. Mara said, "We had him rated very high from a skill set," while also noting, according to ClutchPoints , "We weren't quite sure about the maturity level, but we loved his skill set."

The Giants eventually got another chance to bring McCarthy aboard after he struggled in Minnesota. A 2027 fifth-round draft pick secured his acquisition from the Vikings in September 2026. This move came after quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury, leaving the Giants without a starter.

Welcoming a son in September 2025, he wed his longtime girlfriend in April. These steps happened while he was on the road to recovery from the knee injury that cost him his rookie season.

Mara said, "He's a terrific guy, he's matured, he's married now, has a kid." The executive added that watching McCarthy in practice leaves him impressed. "I'm in awe when I watch him in practice," Mara said. He also noted that McCarthy's physical game has improved, stating, "He's got a much better arm than I thought he ever had," and "He moves around great."

In just three games since arriving in New York, McCarthy has raised his completion percentage to 63.3 and holds a 95.2 passer rating. This marks an improvement of over 22 points compared to his mark from last year.

The Giants will host the Washington Commanders on Thursday, Nov. 12, at 8:15 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium.

articles.title: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski names new starting safety
articles.summary: Kevin Stefanski names Falcons' new starting safety after Jessie Bates trade
articles.body:
Less than 24 hours after losing their sixth game of the season, the Atlanta Falcons executed a trade to send safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a second-round pick in 2027 and a fifth-rounder in 2028.

Bates, a Pro Bowl playmaker known for his elite ball skills, joins an AFC contender in Jacksonville while the Falcons get some draft capital for the future. The move suggests Atlanta is selling at this week's trade deadline, however, head coach Kevin Stefanski said that was not the case during his Monday press conference.

"Obviously, we're not where we want to be, we want to play better, but we're very much in the thick of this thing and we trust in the guys that we have," said Stefanski . "I understand the question, and I understand the question in light of the trade, but in no way, shape or form."

Nonetheless, the Falcons now have a Jesse Bates-sized hole at safety, but Stefanski said DeMarcco Hellams would step into the starting lineup going forward.

"Obviously, DeMarcco is the next man up that we feel really good about," Stefanski said of Bates' replacement.

Hellams and Bates have different playing styles. Bates is more of a free safety, due to his elite range and coverage ability. Meanwhile Hellams is more on the strong safety end. So we expect Xavier Watts to fill some of Bates' role going forward, however, most teams have abandoned the idea of traditional safety roles at this point.

The Falcons drafted Hellams in the seventh round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Alabama. He appeared in 15 games as a rookie, recording 40 tackles (25 solo) and one QB hit. Hellams then missed all of his second season after breaking his ankle during the preseason.

The fourth-year safety is one of former Falcons general manager Terry Fontenot's rare Day 3 draft hits. We would also expect to see defensive back Sydney Brown get some extra reps with Bates out of the picture.

articles.title: Julian Edelman puts Tom Brady on spot with ‘true or false’ Super Bowl question
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have a long road ahead before becoming Super Bowl contenders. However, Tom Brady is already confident about their future. The seven-tim...
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders have a long road ahead before becoming Super Bowl contenders. However, Tom Brady is already confident about their future. The seven-time champion recently made a bold prediction about the franchise , giving Raider Nation hope despite its ongoing rebuild.

According to My Sports Update on X, Brady faced a question from former New England Patriots teammate Julian Edelman during a segment on The Gronk & Jules Show . Edelman asked, "True or false? The Raiders will win the Super Bowl by 2030?" Brady confidently answered, "True," and repeated his response for emphasis. Rob Gronkowski was surprised and joked that he and Edelman could remind Brady of his prediction in 2030 if Las Vegas failed to win it all.

Brady's prediction carries extra weight because he is a minority owner of the Raiders . As an owner, he has a stake in the franchise's future. Las Vegas selected quarterback Fernando Mendoza with the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , hoping he can become its long-term answer under center.

However, the Raiders still have plenty of work to do. Through nine games, Las Vegas holds a 4-5 record and averages 26.4 points per game, but its defense allows 29.8 points per contest. The offense has produced 2,979 total yards, including 2,337 passing yards, but its 642 rushing yards rank near the bottom of the league. Mendoza currently sits behind veteran Kirk Cousins, while young talents Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty offer building blocks for the future. Las Vegas must improve its ground game and defensive consistency to become a legitimate Super Bowl contender.

Brady's prediction may seem ambitious, but the Raiders have until 2030 to prove him right. His bold statement will give Julian Edelman and Rob Gronkowski plenty of material if the franchise falls short.

articles.title: Michael Wilson Injury, Latest Rumors on Cardinals WR's Timeline to Return and Fantasy Impact
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals will be without their top wide receiver for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals will be without their top wide receiver for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, Michael Wilson suffered a neck injury in Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks and will miss the rest of the year.

Meanwhile, quarterback Gardner Minshew is also dealing with an injury that could end his season.

The injury is a huge blow for both the Cardinals and Wilson, who was putting together the best season of his career up to this point. The former third-round pick in 2023 recorded 546 receiving yards and a pair of touchdowns on 51 receptions through the first nine games of the year.

A week ago, against the Dallas Cowboys, he had 111 receiving yards and sent the game to overtime with a touchdown catch in the final seconds.

The injury marks the second key receiver the Cardinals have lost this year. Kendrick Bourne suffered a fractured tibia against the Cowboys and will miss the remainder of the season. Bourne had 26 receptions for 263 yards before the injury.

The remainder of the receivers left on the Cardinals' roster have a combined eight receptions this year.

In terms of fantasy impact, managers who own Trey McBride should expect even more production from him. McBride, one of the best tight ends in the league, has 598 receiving yards and five touchdowns this year, and he'll only get more targets now that Wilson is out for the year.

If fantasy managers choose to replace Wilson with a Cardinals receiver, rookie Reggie Virgil is probably the best bet, though it could be wise to look elsewhere for a replacement.

Some options around the league that may be available include Houston's Tank Dell, San Francisco's Jordan Watkins or Miami's Caleb Douglas.

articles.title: 49ers' Brandon Aiyuk Reinstated by NFL, Details on Roster Exemption Revealed
articles.summary: Brandon Aiyuk is getting closer to making his return to the NFL.
articles.body:
Brandon Aiyuk is getting closer to making his return to the NFL.

Per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero, the San Francisco 49ers receiver has been reinstated from the Reserve/Left Squad list by the NFL, and the team has until Nov. 23 to make a roster move.

Aiyuk has not played in an NFL game since Week 7 of the 2024 season, when he suffered a torn ACL, MCL and Meniscus in his right knee. Last December, he was placed on the Reserve/Left Squad list after he stopped showing up to the team facilities for meetings and rehab work.

He spent his offseason posting lengthy social media rants targeted at the 49ers, other teams, players and even the NFL Players' Association , further tarnishing his hopes of finding a new team.

While being reinstated is one step in the right direction, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones noted last week that it could take "days, weeks or even months" for Aiyuk to return to the field.

Jones cited one source who said Aiyuk would need to be on his "best behavior" when working with the 49ers to find a trade, and the team would have to find another squad that thinks Aiyuk is "worth" trading for.

ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on Saturday the Washington Commanders "haven't completely abandoned" a potential Aiyuk trade, but the team wants to "have discussions with multiple people" before pulling the trigger.

Aiyuk met with the Niners last week, and his agent said the situation is "to be continued."

In his last healthy season in 2023, Aiyuk was at his best, recording 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns in 16 games, helping San Francisco reach the Super Bowl.

But after a severe knee injury and a year away from the game, it's hard to say whether the 28-year-old can ever return to that form. Combine that with his off-the-field behavior, and it makes adding Aiyuk a risky decision for any team.

articles.title: Jordan Davis Traded to Jaguars as Eagles Land NFL Draft Picks After Bates, Godchaux Deals
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars are all in on their pursuit of a Super Bowl title this season.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars are all in on their pursuit of a Super Bowl title this season.

The AFC South team sent the Philadelphia Eagles a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick in exchange for defensive tackle Jordan Davis on Monday.

It was the third defensive trade of the day for the Jaguars, as they also landed safety Jesse Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons and acquired defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero .

Draft picks have not been much of a concern for the Jaguars one day ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported they sent the Falcons a 2027 second-rounder and a 2028 fifth-rounder for Bates, while NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported they sent the Saints a 2028 sixth-rounder that could turn into a 2027 sixth-rounder for Godchaux.

Still, the aggression comes as the Jaguars have an excellent chance to reach the Super Bowl for the first time in franchise history.

They are off to a 6-2 start and are three games ahead of the Houston Texans for first place in the AFC South and the home playoff game that would come with a division title.

They also have no shortage of offensive talent with quarterback Trevor Lawrence leading the way alongside running back Bhayshul Tuten, tight end Brenton Strange, and a group of wide receivers that includes Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers.

Despite the aggressive trades, Jacksonville's defense has also played well and wasn't exactly a glaring weakness. In fact, it is second in the league in points allowed per game (15.1) and is a major reason there are realistic Super Bowl aspirations in place.

And now that defense is even better with a handful of headline players, including Davis.

The defensive tackle helped lead the Eagles to the Super Bowl title during the 2024 campaign and is a force in the middle who can occupy double teams and open up blitzing lanes for outside rushers.

That will be welcome news for Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen, who could see more opportunities for sacks following this move.

Jacksonville also addressed an area of concern with this trade since defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton is expected to miss the remainder of the season with injury. Davis can help fill the void for a Jaguars team that has its eye firmly on the Lombardi Trophy.

articles.summary: The Jaguars have now landed three new defensive players in trades on Monday alone.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars are going all in.

The Jaguars struck a deal to land Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis on Monday afternoon, just a day ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the team announced . In return, the Eagles are getting multiple draft picks, including a first-round selection for next April.

The deal is the third the Jaguars made on Monday to add a defensive player. They acquired safety Jessie Bates III in a trade with the Atlanta Falcons , and also picked up defensive tackle Davon Godchaux in a trade with the New Orleans Saints.

Davis is in his fifth season in the league. He racked up a career-high 72 total tackles and 4.5 sacks during the 2025 campaign, and has 31 total tackles and 1.5 sacks through nine games this season. The 26-year-old, whom the Eagles selected with the No. 13 overall pick in 2022 out of Georgia, signed a three-year, $78 million extension with the Eagles in March.

"We are extremely grateful to Jordan for his contributions to our team on the field and in the Philadelphia community since we drafted him five years ago. He has been a key contributor to our team culture and on-field success, which included two Super Bowl appearances and a world championship in 2024," the Eagles said in a statement . "His growth and development as both a player and a leader are a testament to his hard work and character. We wish Jordan nothing but continued success."

"We are extremely grateful to Jordan for his contributions to our team on the field and in the Philadelphia community since we drafted him five years ago. He has been a key contributor to our team culture and on-field success, which included two Super Bowl appearances and a world championship in 2024," the Eagles said in a statement .

"His growth and development as both a player and a leader are a testament to his hard work and character. We wish Jordan nothing but continued success."

Philadelphia is on a seven-game skid after Sunday's 19-11 loss to the New York Giants. The Eagles (2-7) are last in the NFC East and are all but out of the playoff race this season — especially with quarterback Jalen Hurts sidelined due to blood clots. The latest move gives the Eagles an additional first-round pick in next year's draft and a second-round pick in 2029.

They now have a combined 10 picks in the first two rounds of the next three drafts, including two in the first round in both 2027 and 2028. That should give the organization plenty of room to regroup after this season ends.

Meanwhile, Jacksonville clearly feels like it has a roster capable of making a Super Bowl push, and Monday's moves only bolster that feeling. The three additions will complement an already tough defense that has allowed just 15.1 points per game this season — which is the second-best output in the league behind only the Minnesota Vikings. The Jags sit at 6-2 coming out of Week 9, after they beat the Baltimore Ravens 33-10 for their fifth win in the past six outings.

Jacksonville no longer has a first- or second-round draft pick in 2027 after Monday's transactions, though the Jaguars still hold their first-round picks in 2028 and 2029.

The Jaguars have been to the playoffs only twice in the past nine seasons, and they fell in the wild-card round in 2025, the first under head coach Liam Coen's watch. While Monday's transactions were undoubtedly costly for the franchise, the Jaguars feel ready to go for it and make a legitimate postseason run. Whether that is enough for them to run the table in the AFC and make what would be the team's first Super Bowl remains to be seen.

articles.title: Gardner Minshew Injury Update, Rumors on Surgery & Timeline as Carson Beck Becomes Cardinals QB1
articles.summary: Gardner Minshew's season may be over.
articles.body:
ESPN's Adam Schefter and Josh Weinfuss reported Monday the Arizona Cardinals quarterback may have suffered a torn UCL during the first half of Sunday's loss to the Seattle Seahawks.

While he remained in the game, Schefter noted he is now "seeking additional medical opinions to confirm that he likely will need season-ending surgery."

Arizona responded by reportedly making a move to bolster its quarterback depth:

Minshew had a high completion percentage in Sunday's loss at 21-of-30, but he threw for 166 yards and zero touchdowns while taking three sacks.

The offense managed a mere three points in the 17-3 defeat and was unable to take advantage of a solid performance from the Arizona defense against Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Co.

Arizona already traded Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens after he was benched for Minshew during the team's Week 8 overtime win over the Dallas Cowboys. That means it will likely be Carson Beck time moving forward following the setback to Minshew.

The Cardinals selected Beck with a third-round pick in the 2026 NFL draft after he led Miami to the College Football Playoff national championship game.

Even if Minshew did not suffer the injury, it wouldn't have been surprising if the Cardinals eventually turned to the rookie. After all, Sunday's loss dropped them to 3-6 as the only team in the NFC West under .500.

They are not legitimate contenders this season, so seeing what they have in Beck at some point would have made sense so they could further evaluate the quarterback plans for 2027 and beyond. This only accelerates the timeline and will likely throw him into action during the upcoming game against the Los Angeles Rams.

That means Beck's first career start will come against Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald, which is a daunting proposition.

Still, it will be a chance for the rookie to impress and perhaps help his chances at becoming a starter down the line even when there are more healthy options on the roster.

articles.title: Tom Brady helped raise $450,000 for human trafficking survivors as NFL legend delivers powerful message of hope and support
articles.summary: Tom Brady has spent years making headlines for his achievements on the football field, but his latest appearance brought attention to a cause far removed
articles.body: Tom Brady has spent years making headlines for his achievements on the football field, but his latest appearance brought attention to a cause far removed from the NFL. The seven-time Super Bowl champion joined a major charity fundraiser in New Jersey, helping an organisation dedicated to supporting homeless young people and human trafficking survivors. The event raised more than $450,000, bringing together hundreds of insurance industry leaders. Brady also used the occasion to deliver a heartfelt message about the importance of standing behind young people when they need support the most.Tom Brady joins $450,000 Covenant House fundraiserTom Brady attended Covenant House New Jersey's fundraising event on September 23, 2026, where he took part in a 30-minute conversation with Eric Andersen, president and CEO of AIG. More than 300 insurance industry leaders and professionals attended the gathering, which generated over $450,000 for the organisation.The fundraiser focused on helping young people facing homelessness and survivors of human trafficking. Covenant House New Jersey provides emergency shelter, food, healthcare, education and longer-term housing support. Its programmes also help young people find employment and build independent lives.Brady's appearance brought added attention to the organisation's work, but his message carried a purpose beyond the fundraising total. The former New England Patriots quarterback encouraged attendees to keep supporting vulnerable young people and give them opportunities to build a better future.“Thanks for believing in these young people. Thanks for investing in their future. Keep showing up. Keep believing. That’s how we change lives together.”The event also highlighted the insurance industry's continuing relationship with Covenant House. The sector has supported the organisation through fundraising initiatives for several years. Its September 2024 fundraising dinner, for instance, collected approximately $250,000.Tom Brady highlights importance of supporting homeless youthThe latest fundraiser comes as Covenant House continues to expand its work with vulnerable young people. Its FY2025 impact report revealed that the organisation reached 2,373 young people and provided 95,735 nights of housing. It also served 227 survivors through its human trafficking victim services programme.These figures offer a closer look at why contributions from corporate leaders and public figures matter. Financial support helps the organisation maintain shelters, provide essential services and give young people access to education and employment opportunities.Brady has also maintained a long association with charitable causes throughout his NFL career. His work with Best Buddies International, food banks and disaster relief initiatives has included fundraising appearances and direct contributions.However, his participation in the New Jersey event should not be confused with a personal $450,000 donation. The amount represents the collective funds raised through the fundraiser.For Brady, the appearance offered another opportunity to use his public platform to support a cause affecting young people. His message was simple: lasting change begins when people continue to show up for those who need help.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Rams expect All-Pro WR Puka Nacua to land on injured reserve with multiple knee sprains and turf toe
articles.summary: Head coach Sean McVay made the announcement to reporters on Monday.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams expect to place All-Pro receiver Puka Nacua on injured reserve with MCL and PCL sprains to his right knee and turf toe.

Head coach Sean McVay made the announcement to reporters on Monday. Nacua suffered the injuries during Sunday's 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders. It's not clear how long Nacua will be sidelined, but a stint on injured reserve means he'll miss a minimum of four games.

The news of Nacua's expected IR placement is another significant blow to an offense that's already playing without starting receiver and former Pro Bowler Davante Adams. Now the Rams are facing an extended period without their top two weapons in the passing game.

Nacua was having another All-Pro level season

A two-time All-Pro who led the NFL in receptions (129) and yards per game (107.2) in 2025, Nacua was in the midst of another standout campaign despite having missed two games early in the season.

In seven games this season, Nacua has 70 catches for 715 yards and 4 touchdowns. He had his most productive game of the season against Washington prior to his late-game injury with 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown. He also posted two carries for 20 yards.

Nacua was injured on final Rams snap Sunday

Nacua appeared to sustain his injury on one of those carries on the Rams' final offensive play of the game. He took contact to his knee on a tackle and was able to quickly get up. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported after the game that Nacua sustained an injury and would undergo an MRI on Monday.

Who will step up with Adams and Nacua sidelined?

Adams, meanwhile is sidelined with a ruptured hamstring he sustained in a Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals.

McVay announced on Oct. 19 that Adams was expected to miss six-to-10 weeks with his injury. He's missed three games since. The earliest Adams would return under that timeline would be a Week 12 game against the Green Bay Packers on Dec. 3, while a 10-week absence would keep him out through Week 17 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

The earliest Nacua would be permitted to return from injured reserve would be a Week 15 game against the Dallas Cowboys on Dec. 20.

With both of them sidelined, Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and Jordan Whittington are the next men up on the depth chart. Mumpfield is the leading receiver among the three with 11 catches for 162 yards and a touchdown.

The Rams, meanwhile, are fighting to stay afloat in the NFC playoff picture after entering the season as the favorite to win the Super Bowl. Sunday's win over the Commanders was their third straight and improved their record to 5-4.

That leaves them on the outside looking in at the playoff picture behind the NFC West-leading San Francisco 49ers (7-1) and the 6-3 Packers, who would be the last NFC wild-card team if the playoffs started today.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' $1.4 billion KC Current project faces opposition over $185 million funding deal
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' investment in women's soccer is facing fresh scrutiny as Kansas City moves ahead with a major expansion of the
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' investment in women's soccer is facing fresh scrutiny as Kansas City moves ahead with a major expansion of the Kansas City Current's home stadium. The project has received approval for up to $185 million in public financing, but not everyone on the city council believes the deal offers enough clarity. Three council members raised concerns about the lack of detailed development plans, putting the spotlight on a major project involving the NFL couple's soccer club..Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' KC Current stadium expansion faces oppositionThe Kansas City Current wants to increase CPKC Stadium's capacity from 11,500 to 18,000 seats, creating more room for supporters and potentially attracting larger sporting events. However, the expansion has sparked questions about how much the surrounding community will gain from the city's financial support..Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes are part of the club's ownership group alongside Angie and Chris Long. Brittany joined the original ownership group, while Patrick became a co-owner in January 2023, making him the first active NFL player to hold an ownership stake in an NWSL team.The proposed expansion forms part of a much larger riverfront development plan. Club developer Mukul Sharma said the project could attract up to $800 million in private investment, alongside new housing, commercial spaces and public recreational areas.However, council members Johnathan Duncan, Nathan Willett and Melissa Patterson Hazley opposed the funding agreement. Their concerns centred on the lack of specific development details, particularly what residents would receive in return for the city's financial commitment.Duncan questioned whether the council had enough information to make such a significant decision.“I would love to see a better understanding of what we’re actually getting for our money,” Duncan said.Patterson Hazley also expressed reservations about approving the proposal without a clearer picture of the development.“It felt tantamount to a blank check,” Patterson Hazley said in an email. “I look forward to seeing more specific development plans in the future and I hope to feel comfortable lending my support on bond scheduling. Overall, it’s a worthy project but in my opinion lacked specificity at this stage. I’m ready to learn more.”$185 million KC Current funding deal raises questionsThe financial structure also became a point of disagreement. Duncan warned that redirected tax revenue still carries a cost for the city, even when another entity takes responsibility for the bonds.“I think it’s incumbent upon this body to really consider that these bonds — even if it’s being backed by another entity — isn’t free money,” Duncan said. “We are redirecting revenue that would be going to our general fund back into projects.”Willett separately questioned whether the proposed MODESA 2.0 tax incentive was suitable for an area already experiencing development.Despite the objections, the council approved the agreement. Supporters argued that the Current taking responsibility for issuing the bonds and covering potential debt shortfalls would help protect city finances.The decision moves the stadium expansion forward, but questions about the riverfront's future remain.
