articles.title: Shedeur Sanders has become the Angel Reese of the NFL, thanks to his insufferable supporters
articles.summary: Shedeur Sanders' NFL Draft slide mirrors the Angel Reese playbook as Skip Bayless and Stephen A. Smith turn football criticism into racial controversy.
articles.body: From Skip Bayless accusing NFL teams of racism after the 2025 NFL Draft to ESPN personalities invoking Colin Kaepernick, the Shedeur Sanders discourse looks awfully familiar to anyone who has followed Angel Reese's career in the WNBA. Criticism, of any sort, is seen as a microaggression. The Shedeur Sanders experiment and discourse has become toxic. Legitimate football criticism is apparently a microaggression, NFL general managers are supposedly conspiring against a young quarterback, and anyone who questions the former Colorado star's abilities as a quarterback in the NFL risks being branded more than a hater. They're labeled discriminatory. If Sanders does not get the recognition, playing time or praise fans believe he deserves, those fans scream racism. That should sound very familiar to the way fans and WNBA media have treated the Angel Reese discourse. In my opinion, Sanders has become the Angel Reese of the NFL, not necessarily because of anything the athletes themselves have done on the court or field, or in the media, but because of the exhausting victimhood narratives pushed by some of their most devoted supporters. The similarities are uncanny. Criticize Sanders' decision-making, pocket presence, pre-draft interviews or news conferences? You're racist. Question Reese's offensive efficiency, shot selection or how she compares to Caitlin Clark? Prepare for accusations of racial bias. And heaven forbid you suggest another quarterback deserves an opportunity over Sanders or that Clark is simply a better, more exciting basketball player. For certain corners of sports social media, everything must be viewed through a racial lens. Black versus white. Oppressor versus oppressed. Victim versus villain. They're obsessed with race. It's exhausting, and some prominent sports media personalities have helped pour gasoline on the fire. COLIN KAEPERNICK SAYS NFL IS 'ACTIVELY BLACKBALLING ME' 10 YEARS AFTER KNEELING PROTEST BEGAN Skip Bayless, Stephen A. Smith, & Ryan Clark Turn Sanders' Draft Slide Into a Racial Controversy Remember when Sanders inexplicably fell to the fifth round of the 2025 NFL Draft? The Cleveland Browns eventually selected him with the 144th overall pick, despite considerable pre-draft hype that once placed him in the conversation as a first-round election. Rather than consider that NFL franchises might have legitimate concerns about Sanders' talent, personality, football IQ, work ethic, maturity, or overall fit, some of the biggest names in sports media immediately began suggesting something more sinister. ESPN's Stephen A. Smith was among the loudest. KAEPERNICK TELLS 'THE VIEW' THAT NFL OWNERS KEPT HIM OUT OVER POLITICS AND POWER, CLAIMS THEY DONATE TO TRUMP As Sanders continued falling down draft boards, Smith suggested the situation resembled the NFL's controversial treatment of former San Francisco 49ers quarterback Colin Kaepernick. Smith declared, "This feels like (Colin) Kaepernick-level collusion." He also accused NFL owners of appearing to collude against Sanders and suggested teams were motivated by their dislike of his father, Deion Sanders. Think about that. Thirty-two NFL franchises making their own personnel decisions somehow became evidence of a coordinated effort to keep Sanders down, in part because of his race, allegedly. And Smith wasn't alone. Skip Bayless initially described Sanders' draft slide as the most disgusting development in NFL Draft history. Then, following Sanders' impressive preseason debut against the Carolina Panthers in August 2025, Bayless took things considerably further. "Tonight, Shedeur Sanders made the entire National Football League look like a whole bunch of petty fools and, in some cases, racist fools." Bayless also accused teams of being motivated by their dislike of Deion Sanders, arguing that Shedeur had embarrassed the organizations that passed on him. There was just one glaring problem: Bayless didn't provide evidence establishing that any NFL team passed on Sanders because of his race. Apparently, one strong preseason performance was enough to expose an alleged league-wide racial conspiracy. Former ESPN analyst Ryan Clark also brought race into the conversation before the draft, suggesting that Sanders faced additional scrutiny because he was a confident Black quarterback, something many Sanders fans have echoed online throughout the last two seasons. Clark argued that Sanders' appearance, bravado, and skin color contributed to the criticism surrounding him. They willfully chose to ignore the legitimate football-related explanations for his slide and pushed the black victim narrative. CBS Sports NFL insider Jonathan Jones reported concerns about how Sanders handled the pre-draft process, while other reporting highlighted questions surrounding his interviews, preparation, and ability to transition to the professional game. Former NFL quarterback Boomer Esiason even reported that some teams had removed Sanders from their draft boards entirely. Could NFL teams have misjudged Sanders? Sure. Could they have overreacted to his personality or the attention surrounding his famous father? Plausible. But being evaluated incorrectly isn't automatically discrimination. Sometimes teams simply don't believe a player is worth the investment, especially in the early rounds. That's how the NFL Draft works. The Angel Reese Playbook: When Basketball Criticism Becomes a Racial Controversy If you've followed the WNBA since Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese entered the league, you've already watched a similar spectacle unfold. Clark and Reese have been linked since their memorable college basketball battles, but some supporters have transformed their rivalry into something far more divisive than basketball. For certain Reese defenders, criticism of her offensive game, including mentioning her uncanny ability to rebound her own misses, humorously trademarking "MeBounds," is treated not merely as an opinion about basketball skill, but as a potential indictment of the critic's racial attitudes. Meanwhile, praise for Clark can become entangled in arguments about racial privilege and the treatment of Black women in professional sports. ESPN's Monica McNutt helped illustrate just how quickly the conversation can shift. Following Clark's flagrant foul against Reese in May 2025, McNutt discussed allegations of racist fan behavior and questioned how differently the incident would have been received had Reese committed the foul. McNutt argued that the two athletes were being placed into opposing roles, with one portrayed as a victim and the other as someone needing protection. Her comments were part of a broader discussion about racial double standards, but they also demonstrated how quickly a basketball play can become a referendum on race. The race card is pulled in almost every controversial play and action Reese has been involved in. The controversy became even more revealing when the WNBA investigated allegations of hateful fan comments and "monkey noises" directed toward Reese during that same Fever vs Sky game. The league ultimately announced that its investigation could not substantiate the specific allegations. Even WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert found herself under fire in September 2024 when she discussed the commercial appeal of the Clark-Reese rivalry without initially delivering the condemnation of racist fan behavior that several players and the players' union wanted. The backlash was substantial, with prominent players including DiJonai Carrington criticizing her response. Engelbert subsequently clarified that racism and hatred had no place in the league. More often than not, situations involving Angel Reese have become a racial grievance. It's nauseating. Dillon Gabriel Versus Shedeur Sanders: Another Manufactured Racial Controversy And now we have the Dillon Gabriel vs Shedeur Sanders situation. Sanders and Gabriel entered the Cleveland Browns' quarterback room under dramatically different circumstances. Gabriel was selected in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft, while Sanders had to wait until the fifth. For some Sanders supporters, that draft order itself became another reason to question whether the NFL was treating their favorite quarterback fairly based on race. The rivalry has also provided endless ammunition for social media arguments about which quarterback deserves opportunities and whether Cleveland has handled Sanders appropriately. Instead of allowing Gabriel and Sanders to compete as quarterbacks based on meritocracy, some fans seemed determined to make their competition about something bigger. Every compliment directed toward Gabriel becomes a potential slight against Sanders. Every criticism of Sanders becomes an opportunity to question the motivations of coaches, executives, or media members. It's the same exhausting dynamic surrounding Clark and Reese. Rather than simply acknowledging that two athletes have different strengths, weaknesses, and accomplishments, some supporters insist on turning the conversation into a moral crusade. Athletes Don't Need to Be Victims to Be Worth Supporting Here's what makes this entire controversy so ridiculous: Shedeur Sanders and Angel Reese don't need these narratives to justify their places in professional sports. Sanders was a productive college quarterback who earned an opportunity in the NFL. Reese became a national champion at LSU and established herself as a formidable rebounder, and many times this season, an effective scorer in the WNBA. Their accomplishments are legitimate, but so are criticisms of their games. Sanders can be a talented quarterback who still has weaknesses that NFL coaches and GMs must evaluate. Reese can be an outstanding rebounder whose offensive efficiency deserves scrutiny. Neither observation is inherently racist. Neither athlete needs supporters inventing ulterior motives every time someone offers an unfavorable assessment. The irony is that the constant racial framing can ultimately undermine the very athletes their fans claim to defend. Instead of discussing Sanders' development as a quarterback, we're debating whether NFL executives are racists. Instead of discussing Reese's rebounding, scoring, or defensive impact, we're debating whether someone praising Clark is participating in racial favoritism. It's a disservice to both athletes. And when media personalities with enormous platforms amplify accusations without presenting sufficient evidence, they make the discourse even worse. Sports fans should be able to criticize players without being subjected to a trial over their character. They should be able to support Gabriel, or in this season's case, Deshaun Watson, without hating Sanders, or celebrate Clark without harboring animosity toward Reese. Actual racism deserves condemnation. Actual discrimination deserves investigation. But disagreement is not discrimination, criticism is not persecution, and losing a competition is not proof of a conspiracy. Unfortunately, that's a message some of the loudest Sanders and Reese supporters desperately need to hear. Because the more they insist that every setback is evidence of racial injustice, the more they turn two accomplished athletes into perpetual victims in a culture war neither needs to win. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP A Response to Sanders Supporters When I see Sanders fans in my replies say things like, "ANY black athlete that has confidence and swagger makes white nationalist males uncomfortable I’m starting to see," I immediately roll my eyes. These fans can't understand that Shedeur may come across to many people as immature, self-absorbed at times, and lacking self-awareness when he seemingly disrespects the Saints defense when he's about to make his first start of the season. Disagree all you want, but his actions, including his arrogance he's displayed at times, along with his play are why so many teams passed on him in the NFL Draft. Let this sink in. Out of 42 eligible quarterback last season, Shedeur Sanders ranked 41st in Passer Rating. He threw more interceptions than touchdowns. He had the fifth-worst QBR since QBR became a stat in 2006, making it the worst for any Browns QB with at least six starts in the history of the franchise. My criticism is not racism. I could lay out why I believe Watson is the best option as starter for the Cleveland Browns, but we'll save that for another article. All in all, my thoughts are based on what I see on the field and my opinion of what I hear from him off of it, which seems to be echoed by NFL front office and some media members. The stats don't lie. You supporter do.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni denies flipping off Eagles fans after home loss to Giants as skid continues: 'Absolutely not'
articles.summary: The Eagles have now dropped seven straight after Sunday's 19-11 loss to the New York Giants.
articles.body:
No, Nick Sirianni did not intentionally give Philadelphia Eagles fans the middle finger while walking into the tunnel at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday afternoon.

The Eagles head coach said he was stunned when he was informed of that speculation following Philadelphia's 19-11 loss to the New York Giants on Sunday. That gesture, Sirianni insisted, was not something he intentionally did in the wake of what was a seventh straight loss.

"Absolutely not," Sirianni said, via ESPN's Tim McManus . "That was a surprise to me, but absolutely not."

It is easy to understand why Eagles fans may be frustrated with Sirianni. The Eagles (2-7) have lost seven straight games now, and sit last in the NFC East. They are all but out of the postseason race this fall, and the team looks incredibly different than the one that won the Super Bowl two seasons ago. They've lost quarterback Jalen Hurts due to blood clots, too, and have been struggling since.

Assuming the Eagles don't miraculously rally the rest of the way, this will be just the second time in the past decade that they didn't make the postseason. They've won two Super Bowl titles in that span.

On Sunday, as Sirianni left the field, his right hand was moving around a bit awkwardly as he walked past fans and into the tunnel. That led to speculation about the middle finger gesture, though Sirianni never looked anywhere but forward and definitely didn't make a clear gesture. His demeanor on the walk in question never changed.

Sirianni has a history of yelling at fans, including an incident in which he apologized after shouting at a group of Eagles fans during a 2024 game with the Cleveland Browns. But Sunday's exit from the field wasn't even close to that.

The Eagles are entering their bye week, and will return Nov. 22 for a matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers. They dealt defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Monday, in return for a first-round draft pick next spring and a second-round selection in 2029. They now have a combined 10 picks in the first two rounds of the next three drafts, which should give them plenty of room to regroup after this season ends.

Until then, Sirianni will attempt to get the Eagles back on track during the final stretch of the season. He didn't rule out any coaching changes, either, but that's not his focus just yet.

"Right now we're going through the self-scout process," Sirianni said. "Guys are working on studies right now, and we're determined to figure things out and get on the right track, and that's what we're worried about right at this particular time."

articles.title: NFL reinstates WR Brandon Aiyuk from reserve/left squad list, leaving 49ers with a decision
articles.summary: Kyle Shanahan, meanwhile, maintained his indifference regarding Aiyuk, telling reporters that Monday's transaction "means absolutely nothing to our team."
articles.body:
The NFL has reinstated San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk from the league's reserve/left squad list. The league made the announcement on its transaction wire Monday.

Per NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the NFL also granted the 49ers a two-week roster exemption, meaning they'll have two weeks to make a roster move in response to Aiyuk's new status. They'll have the option of either releasing him, trading him or adding Aiyuk to the 53-man roster.

Keeping Aiyuk in San Francisco is not believed to be on the table as the 49ers and Aiyuk have been in conflict since his unexcused departure from the team led to his placement on the reserve/left squad list in December 2025. San Francisco's management has repeatedly made it clear Aiyuk is not welcome back with the team.

The league granted Aiyuk's reinstatement in response to his request last week through his new agent, Drew Rosenhaus . Aiyuk is attempting to make an NFL comeback, having not played since Week 7 of the 2024 season. He could have filed for reinstatement at any time during his absence from the 49ers.

What about the $13M the 49ers want back?

Reportedly at issue regarding his resolution with the 49ers is a $13 million roster bonus the 49ers previously paid out and believed they are owed. The 49ers reportedly claim the money is due because of Aiyuk's refusal to show up in 2025 to team facilities or to rehabilitation appointments for the ACL, MCL and meniscus tears he sustained during the 2024 season.

Rosenhaus said last week he and Aiyuk were meeting with the 49ers on Friday in an attempt to resolve the situation.

"We will put our best foot forward and go from there," Rosenhaus told ESPN .

Per ESPN, that meeting lasted about 75 minutes, with Rosenhuaus saying afterward, "To be continued."

Aiyuk, meanwhile, said this to reporters prior to the meeting:

"I'm feeling great, feeling healthy," Aiyuk said. "It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process, but I'm back to 100% and looking to get reinstated to the National Football League."

It's not clear as of Monday's transaction how or if the 49ers and Aiyuk resolved the issue of the $13 million bonus or anything else. The 49ers previously voided $27 million in 2026 guarantees in Aiyuk's contract.

49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters last week he had "no clue" what was going on with Aiyuk and that he "could care less."

"It means absolutely nothing to our team," Shanahan said when asked about the roster exemption, per ESPN. "I think we got a two-week roster exemption and that's all administrative stuff to me."

articles.title: Cardinals reportedly fear QB Gardner Minshew has torn UCL, could miss remainder of season
articles.summary: Minshew played through the injury in Arizona's loss to Seattle last week.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals are awaiting additional tests on quarterback Gardner Minshew's elbow.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the concern is that the QB has torn the UCL in his throwing elbow and would miss the rest of the season, with months of rehab ahead.

If Minshew is out for the rest of the season, rookie quarterback Carson Beck, the Cardinals' third-round draft pick this year, would be in line to start.

On the final play of the first half of the Seahawks' 17-3 win, Donte Fowler hit Minshew coming around the offensive line. The quarterback was in the middle of throwing, and his arm bent at an odd angle as he forced the pass.

Beck started warming up, but Minshew didn't miss any snaps in the game.

The loss against Seattle was Minshew's first start of the season, after he replaced Jacoby Brissett in the team's comeback overtime win over the Dallas Cowboys. Minshew has thrown for 354 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions in two games this year.

Minshew's promotion to starter also came after Brissett was traded to the Baltimore Ravens last week.

With Beck as the only other quarterback in Arizona's organization, the team is reportedly signing career backup Josh Johnson off the Cleveland Browns' practice squad, per ESPN's Adam Schefter . The Cardinals will be Johnson's 15th NFL team in his 14-year career.

Beck has not yet played in a regular season game. The rookie played extensively in Arizona's first preseason action against the Carolina Panthers in the Hall of Fame Game.

The quarterback completed 15 of 19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown, with no interceptions, in the loss to the Panthers. Beck suffered a rib injury during the game that sidelined him for the rest of the preseason.

Minshew isn't the only potential season-ending injury that Arizona is dealing with. Wide receiver Michael Wilson fractured something in his neck , according to head coach Mike LaFleur, and will miss the remainder of the season.

The Cardinals play the Los Angeles Rams this week. Arizona then has the Kansas City Chiefs, Washington Commanders and Philadelphia Eagles, then a Week 14 bye.

Arizona is 3-6 and last in the NFC West. With the trade decisions made earlier in the year and the high-profile injuries suffered last week, the rest of the season may be an evaluation of the team's young talent.

articles.title: Sean McVay Addresses Trade Possibilities After Puka Nacua Injury amid NFL Rumors Before Deadline
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams were previously expected to have a quiet trade deadline, but a key injury this week may have changed their plans.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams were previously expected to have a quiet trade deadline , but a key injury this week may have changed their plans.

Wide receiver Puka Nacua is heading to the injured reserve with MCL and PCL sprains plus turf toe, meaning he'll miss at least four games. Head coach Sean McVay said on Monday that the team will reconsider making a trade ahead of Tuesday's deadline.

"Yeah, I think you look at all avenues," McVay told reporters . "I think you've got to look at all avenues to try to be able to solve some of the issues or situations or scenarios that have come up. And so a lot of new things that occur on a daily basis, and so I would never rule it out."

Wide receiver Davante Adams landed on the injured reserve after the Rams' Week 6 contest against the Arizona Cardinals and won't be able to return until at least Nov. 25, though his timeline to return is six to 10 weeks, so it could be even longer.

That puts Los Angeles in a tricky situation as it tries to reach the playoffs.

There should be a handful of wide receivers available for the Rams to target, like the Indianapolis Colts' Josh Downs or the Jacksonville Jaguars' Brian Thomas Jr. Los Angeles could also aim for a smaller name just to get some relief until its stars are back.

The Rams started the season 2-4 but have since won three straight games and are looking more like the contenders they were expected to be coming into the season.

The injuries to Nacua and Adams will make keeping their momentum alive difficult, though.

articles.title: Rhamondre Stevenson Injured, Latest Rumors on Patriots RB and Fantasy Outlook, Depth Chart
articles.summary: The New England Patriots and fantasy football managers alike may need to turn elsewhere for the immediate future with running back Rhamondre Stevenson reportedly dealing with a knee injury.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots and fantasy football managers alike may need to turn elsewhere for the immediate future with running back Rhamondre Stevenson reportedly dealing with a knee injury.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Monday the veteran "is dealing with a knee tendon issue that is not expected to require surgery but could sideline him for a short period of time."

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport added more context:

It is another setback for the New England running back room, as TreVeyon Henderson missed the last two games with an illness.

ESPN's Mike Reiss noted the depth chart is now Corey Kiner and Lan Larison ahead of Terrell Jennings, who is on the practice squad.

From a fantasy perspective, managers who are completely desperate for running back options because of injuries or bye weeks could look at Kiner and Larison as waiver-wire pickups. After all, the Patriots have to play someone at the position with Stevenson and Henderson sidelined, and they are the next ones up.

And if that is the case, Kiner is the obvious choice.

He has at least seen some limited action this season with 50 carries for 244 yards and one touchdown. He impressed against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday with 55 yards and a score on the ground and will surely see plenty of opportunities against the Detroit Lions.

As for Larison, he has just three carries on the season.

The bigger question is how long the Patriots will be without Stevenson in the middle of a playoff race. The loss to the Packers dropped them to 5-4 on the season, which is good enough for the seventh and final seed in the AFC playoff picture.

They are tied with the Cleveland Browns and one game ahead of the Las Vegas Raiders and Baltimore Ravens, so just treading water without Stevenson may not be good enough to make the postseason.

Stevenson hasn't even been that effective as a runner this season at just 3.9 yards per carry, which is tied for the lowest mark of his career. But he is a physical runner who can pick up the difficult yardage while remaining involved in the aerial attack with 26 catches for 258 yards and two scores.

His presence will take the pressure off quarterback Drake Maye when he returns, but the Patriots will have to rely on Kiner in the meantime.

articles.title: Josh Allen reveals how Hailee Steinfeld and their new baby have changed his daily routine in rare interview
articles.summary: Josh Allen has a new bedtime routine, and it no longer involves much television.
articles.body: Josh Allen has a new bedtime routine, and it no longer involves much television. The Buffalo Bills quarterback and his wife, Hailee Steinfeld, welcomed daughter Harper Haize Allen in April 2026. Seven months later, Allen is talking about what that change looks like day to day, down to the minute. In an interview published November 5 for The Healthy’s “How I Healthspan” series, he covered sleep, screen time, his love of sweets and the recovery tools he leans on during the NFL season. For a player who rarely shares home life, it was a candid look.How fatherhood has changed Josh Allen’s nights at homeThe biggest shift is the quiet part of the evening. Once Harper is asleep, Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld give themselves about 35 to 40 minutes to watch something, unwind and talk. Allen said, “There’s definitely been less TV now.” He sees real value in easing into bed without a screen in his face, and he made it clear he does not miss the old habit.That window is small. In season, a quarterback’s days fill up fast with meetings, treatment and practice, and a newborn takes whatever remains. So half an hour of conversation with his wife carries weight. It is the one stretch of the day that belongs to the two of them.For readers trying to copy any of it, the easy one is the screen cutback. It costs nothing, and Allen finds it beneficial.The Healthy’s series centers on health habits, and Allen’s installment leaned toward routines rather than football. Sleep came up, or the lack of it. Getting used to fewer hours is now part of his life with Harper.Allen is not a public oversharer. Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift live much of their relationship in front of cameras, but Allen and Steinfeld mostly keep theirs private. So even a detail as plain as a nightly TV window stands out.Josh Allen’s sweet tooth and favorite recovery toolsAllen was just as open about food. Chocolate chip cookies are his weak spot, and he said they get the better of him. No quarterback’s plan is spotless, and his has a cookie-shaped hole in it. Lately he has swapped them for fruit at dessert. He admitted that probably is not the best choice, but in his mind it beats a cookie.Recovery is where he gets more specific, and the list is short.He called the sauna the best tool he has, by a wide margin. His Therabody Theragun gets heavy use too. Next on the list is the Ammortal Chamber, a newer setup the Bills have been trying out. Allen said he plans to give it a go.Put together, it shows a quarterback managing two schedules. One runs on game weeks and treatment slots. The other runs on a baby’s needs, which do not care about either.Away from the training room, the family has had a busy few weeks. Allen and Steinfeld marked Harper’s first Halloween, and they also hosted their annual Halloween party for the Bills after the bye week. articles.title: 'Disappointed,' Jordan Davis Reacts to Surprise Eagles Trade to Jaguars Before 2027 NFL Deadline
articles.summary: Jordan Davis' time with the Philadelphia Eagles came to an end after four and a half years on Monday.
articles.body:
Jordan Davis' time with the Philadelphia Eagles came to an end after four and a half years on Monday.

The defensive tackle was traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars in return for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick. Davis admitted that the news was disappointing, but he understood why the Eagles decided to trade him.

"I'm a little disappointed, but, you know, I understand that they're in the rebuilding process," he said. "For the picks, first-round, second-round picks, obviously, it helps the team. I love those guys, so however it can help the team, even in my departure, I'm actually really glad to be doing that."

Davis was a first-round pick by the Eagles in 2022 and helped them reach the Super Bowl in his first season in Philadelphia, though they came up short against the Kansas City Chiefs. Two years later, he helped the Birds win it all, picking up a sack in the Super Bowl against the Chiefs.

Davis is coming off the best season of his career, in which he recorded 72 tackles, 4.5 sacks and six passes defended. He's had a solid start to the 2026 campaign, picking up 31 tackles and 1.5 sacks through nine games.

While Davis made it clear he was happy in Philadelphia, it was probably the best decision for the Eagles to move on from one of their top players on defense as they moved toward a rebuild.

Philadelphia started the season 2-0 but has since dropped seven consecutive games, losing starting quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season along the way. Even if the Eagles can rally and reach the playoffs, they simply don't have the roster to compete for a Super Bowl and have seemingly decided to wave the white flag.

Leaving his home in Philadelphia will be tough, but Davis is entering into a great situation in Jacksonville.

The Jaguars are 6-2 with a handful of impressive wins and appear capable of reaching the Super Bowl for the first time in franchise history. They've been aggressive ahead of Tuesday's deadline, adding safety Jessie Bates from the Atlanta Falcons and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints before the trade for Davis.

Whether those moves will pay off remains to be seen.

articles.title: Tony Romo makes surprise appearance on Pat McAfee’s MNF altcast
articles.summary: The sports world hasn’t seen a lot of Tony Romo since he was placed on leave and eventually let go from his position in the No. 1 NFL booth at CBS alongside...
articles.body:
The sports world hasn't seen a lot of Tony Romo since he was placed on leave and eventually let go from his position in the No. 1 NFL booth at CBS alongside Jim Nantz following his OWI charge and the subsequent video of his sobriety test that came out over the summer.

Other than a few statements and a brief appearance at a PGA Q-School event , Romo has largely kept quiet through the start of the NFL season.

But that all changed on Monday night, when Romo joined Pat McAfee's Monday Night Football ESPN2 altcast via video as the Minnesota Vikings hosted the Buffalo Bills.

McAfee introduced Romo as a "quarterback expert" and aimed a light joke at ESPN's Dan Orlovsky, who was working the sidelines along with McAfee.

Through his time on the altcast which crossed nearly five minutes of game time, Romo offered some general analysis on the game action so far, complimenting Brian Flores and the defense of the Vikings.

He also did a bit of his quarterback cadence, joking that the Vikings needed to get the ball more to star receiver Justin Jefferson.

At the end of his appearance, McAfee thanked Romo for appearing on the show, saying, "We missed the hell out of you this season. You need to know that from all of us. We appreciate you, brother."

While McAfee was seemingly trying to sign off, Romo made sure to get one more bit of analysis in before leaving the show.

While seeing Romo at all at this point comes as something of a shock given how absent he has been from this NFL season after holding such a prominent role in broadcasting over the past few years, it's not that surprising that appearing with McAfee would be one of his first stops. McAfee offers an extremely safe entry point for Romo, where he can be sure going into his appearance that he will be talking strictly football and won't be asked any unsavory questions about the past few months that he might not be comfortable answering.

The appearance also comes at an interesting moment for ESPN, as the network appears to be in the process of a dragged-out breakup with Troy Aikman , who has worked alongside play-by-play man Joe Buck for more than two decades dating back to their time together at Fox. While Greg Olsen, currently in the No. 2 booth at Fox, is widely seen as the leader in the race to potentially replace Aikman , Monday's appearance at least shows that McAfee might be in Romo's camp, and the power that McAfee has at ESPN is tough to overstate.

At the very least, this first appearance does indicate that Romo is ready to start his comeback into the public eye. Maybe that comes with more appearances with McAfee, either on future altcasts or on his eponymous show on ESPN. It would certainly be a sensible next step.

articles.title: Ex-Chiefs OL proposes trade sending Vikings WR Justin Jefferson to KC
articles.summary: Ex-Chiefs OL Mitchell Schwartz wants Kansas City to send the Vikings a king’s ransom at the 2026 NFL trade deadline for star WR Justin Jefferson.
articles.body:
Ex- Kansas City Chiefs offensive lineman Mitchell Schwartz took to Twitter on November 9 to propose a massive deal that would send a king's ransom to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for superstar wide receiver Justin Jefferson at the 2026 NFL trade deadline.

Schwartz's creative trade package included "at least" two first-round picks and a third-round selection, which would hamstring Kansas City's flexibility in the NFL draft for the foreseeable future.

While it is unclear exactly how serious Schwartz was about this hypothetical scenario, the Chiefs are rumored to be among the teams exploring options at the wide receiver position ahead of the NFL trade deadline on November 10.

Jefferson isn't expected to be among the wide receivers who will be available on the trade market tomorrow, but Schwartz's comment comes as rumors are circulating that Kansas City's front office wants to add a veteran pass-catcher at some point before the 3 p.m. CT deadline.

articles.title: Packers look like true Super Bowl contenders after dominating Patriots, and Micah Parsons isn’t even back yet
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers have turned things around in dramatic fashion after a slow start that saw them lose two of their first three games. Instead of sinking...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers have turned things around in dramatic fashion after a slow start that saw them lose two of their first three games. Instead of sinking to the bottom of the division, the Packers have served notice that they just may be the best team in the NFC North and will have a legitimate chance to represent the NFC in the Super Bowl in mid-February.

Green Bay has won five of its last six games, and while the Packers still sit in fourth place in the division, a legitimate question can be asked after the Packers just took apart the defending AFC champion New England Patriots by an overwhelming 45-27 margin.

Just who is going to beat the Packers going forward?

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The schedule ahead is challenging, but the Packers are not about to back down from any of the upcoming opponents. They host the offensively deficient Vikings in Week 10 and then have their bye week. They had the Vikings on the ropes in Week 1 before Minnesota surged in the final quarter and stole the opener. This time the Packers get the Vikings at Lambeau.

The Rams and Saints follow on the road, and neither has played up to expectations this year. A shootout with the Bills and Allen follow in Week 14.

Once that game is over, the Packers will know exactly where they stand. They could have Micah Parsons back in the lineup by then, and that could give Green Bay an unstoppable characteristic.

Dominant offensive performances that few teams could match

The win over the Patriots was their most impressive of the season because quarterback Jordan Love delivered a peak performance and looked as good as any quarterback in the league, including Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills or Joe Burrow of the Cincinnati Bengals.

Four weeks earlier, the Packers had delivered another impressive victory, taking apart the much-praised Chicago Bears by a 31-7 score. While the Bears did not have Caleb Williams in the lineup in that game, Love and his crew of receivers torched the Chicago defense with little trouble.

A deeper look at both of those games demonstrated what makes the Packers so dangerous. In the win over the Bears at Lambeau Field, Love completed 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards with 2 touchdowns and no interceptions. His primary partners in that game were wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson is a burner and Golden is even faster. Watson caught 6 of 8 targets for 143 yard and 2 TDs, while Golden brought in 6 of 7 passes for 123 yards.

Love showed off his ability to deliver the deep pass as he hit Watson with a 53-yarder and Golden with a 50-yarder.

In the win over the Patriots, it was much the same thing in a much tougher environment, Love had another monster game. He completed 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards with 3 TDs while keeping it clean on the interception side of the ledger. He also ran 13 yards for the opening touchdown of the game.

Once again, it was the 1-2 punch of Watson and Golden that supplied much of the damage to the New England second. Both receivers got the best of Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez, a Pro Bowl performer and one of the best at his position in the league. Watson caught 7 of 9 targets for 171 yards with 1 TD, as he averaged 24.4 yards per catch. Golden caught all 10 of his targets and he had 164 receiving yards and 1 TD.

Packers have an elite QB at the top of his game

Head coach Matt LaFleur said that Love has been doing everything the coaching staff has asked of him.

"I can't say enough great things about him," LaFleur said , per Matt Schneidman of The Athletic . "What's even better about him is just how he is on a daily basis. Just coming in, working with him, he is the same guy every day, whether it's a great performance like he's been doing consistently or (not). He's just the same guy. He's the same guy that we got when we drafted him, and I think it's a big-time credit and I don't want that to get overlooked."

Consistency has been the key to the Packers quarterback. Even though Green Bay has gotten very little out of its running attack, there is an unstoppable characteristic to the passing game.

In addition to the offense, they are playing solid defense. The Packers are giving up 21.2 points per game , ranking 11th in the NFL.

Safety Evan Williams is on his way to an All-Pro season 76 tackles, 7 passes defensed, 3 interceptions, 2 tackles for loss and 1 fumble recovery. Linebacker Isasiah McDuffie is also playiing extremely well with 53 stops, 1 sack, 3 TFL, 2 forced fumbles and 2 fumble recoveries.

A good defense has a chance to become great once the elite pass-rush ability of Parsons returns to this unit. The Packers are growing every week, and they just may not stop until they get a chance to fight for the NFL's most prized possession — the Vince Lombardi Trophy.

articles.title: Steelers HC Mike McCarthy gives ‘practical and realistic’ take on surprising 6-2 start
articles.summary: Mike McCarthy is proud of the Pittsburgh Steelers’ winning momentum, but the head coach maintained a realistic stance on the team’s ceiling midway through t...
articles.body:
Mike McCarthy is proud of the Pittsburgh Steelers ' winning momentum, but the head coach maintained a realistic stance on the team's ceiling midway through the 2026 NFL season.

McCarthy is going through his first year as the Steelers' head coach, helping the franchise start a new era following Mike Tomlin's retirement. It has been a promising start as Pittsburgh is firmly in the playoff race of the AFC bracket.

McCarthy spoke with media on Monday as Pittsburgh rested on a bye throughout Week 9. Preparing for Week 10, the head coach is happy to see the team boasting a winning record after eight games. However, the job is not complete as he was blunt on the team achieving success this season.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I'm also practical and realistic. You don't win anything after 8 games," McCarthy said, per reporter Chris Adamski.

Mike McCarthy has the Steelers in playoff contention. However, with Aaron Rodgers playing his last year in the NFL, the head coach looks to lead the team to a deep playoff run to send the Hall of Fame quarterback off into the sunset.

Pittsburgh has a 6-2 record this season, controlling the top spot in the AFC North Division standings. They are above the Cincinnati Bengals, the Cleveland Browns and the Baltimore Ravens at the moment. In terms of the conference standings, they are fourth place. They lead over the Kansas City Chiefs and the Bengals while being under the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Denver Broncos.

Rodgers has completed 175 passes for 1,871 yards and 13 touchdowns and six interceptions so far after eight games. Jaylen Warren leads the run game with 119 carries for 704 yards and two touchdowns while catching 25 passes for 294 yards and a touchdown. DK Metcalf tops receivers with 33 catches for 378 yards and a touchdown, while Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth has seven touchdowns combined.

The Steelers will begin preparations for their next matchup, being on the road. They take on the Bengals in Week 10 as kickoff commences on Nov. 15 at 8:20 p.m. ET.
